BlockIn.description:
A block as the node's JSON shows it: `text` (markdown), `try` (question) or `callout`
(callout, title, markdown).
BlockIn.title: BlockIn

ChecklistOut.description: The checklist, and the problems behind it, so Checks is one request (M4K.6).
ChecklistOut.title: ChecklistOut

DraftOut.description:
The node, or null with `problems` when its latest revision no longer reads against the
index's registries (#173).
DraftOut.title: DraftOut

EventOut.description: One entry of a draft's log (M4R.5).
EventOut.title: EventOut

FilesOut.description: A revision's files, exactly as they would land; `exam_yaml` is empty without a pool.
FilesOut.title: FilesOut

GivenIn.description:
An option's index for a choice, a number for a number. Taken as any JSON value, so that
`true` or "1" reach the grader and are refused as CA0218, not coerced.
GivenIn.title: GivenIn

InviteOut.description: What an invitee sees before signing up.
InviteOut.title: InviteOut

Level.description: T10.1's five. A level describes a node, never a learner.
Level.title: Level

MemberOut.description: A member, named by public id; the integer key never leaves the database (M4A.1).
MemberOut.title: MemberOut

Message.description: An error answer: the sentence a person reads, and its diagnostic code (spec M4D.4).
Message.title: Message

NeighbourOut.description: A neighbour as a card: enough for a node page's side panel (L5) without another request.
NeighbourOut.title: NeighbourOut

OpenIn.description: An indexed node's id; or a new node's id with its first fields.
OpenIn.title: OpenIn

ProblemOut.description: One problem, as `code-schema validate` reports it; `text` is its printed line.
ProblemOut.title: ProblemOut

QuestionOut.description:
A try question, its answer included: it is formative, and the page checks it (M3P1.4).

`options` for a choice; `answer`, a number with its unit and tolerance or a sequence's text
with what else it accepts; `steps` for an order, in the right order — the page shuffles them
(M4.8c spec, M4Q.5). Exam questions (T7.1) are scored, and their answers never leave the
server.
QuestionOut.title: QuestionOut

RefusedOut.description:
A refusal: why, every problem the draft's files would have (M4W.3), and for a checklist
that fails, its items (M4.5 spec, M4R.6).
RefusedOut.title: RefusedOut

ResourceOut.description: One entry of the Learn it section (M3P1.2). Our sentence and a link, never their text.
ResourceOut.title: ResourceOut

ResultOut.description: A candidate as the Start board's *Is this what you mean?* panel shows it (L1).
ResultOut.title: ResultOut

ReviewQuestionOut.description:
One question of the submitted revision, as its reviewer sees it: the key and rationale only
once they have answered it (M4R.4). A choice is answered by its option's index.
ReviewQuestionOut.title: ReviewQuestionOut

Role.description: In rank order: each role includes the ones before it.
Role.title: Role

SequenceBlockOut.description: DNA, RNA or protein letters, drawn in groups of ten (M4.8c spec, M4Q.2).
SequenceBlockOut.title: SequenceBlockOut

SideCardOut.description: A neighbour on the node page, with its time: the L5 side column's *level · N min*.
SideCardOut.title: SideCardOut

StopOut.description: A stop as the Route board draws it (L4), with why it is on this route (M2P2.2).
StopOut.title: StopOut

StudioExamQuestionOut.description:
An exam question as the builder edits it (M4Q.5): its stem as blocks and as the text the
file holds, and whether the live index holds it unchanged.
StudioExamQuestionOut.title: StudioExamQuestionOut

StudioQuestionOut.description:
A try question; `options` for a choice, `answer` with unit and tolerance for a number, or
as text with `accept` and `exact` for a sequence; `steps` for an order (M4Q.5).
StudioQuestionOut.title: StudioQuestionOut

TryBlockOut.description: Where a try question sits; the question itself is in `questions`.
TryBlockOut.title: TryBlockOut

VerifyOut.description: `clean` when no problem refuses; warnings may still be listed (M4W.5).
VerifyOut.title: VerifyOut

post.description:
Put the invite in the session; sign-up through allauth then reads it (M4A.2).

It changes the session, so it needs the CSRF token, though no account: otherwise a third-party
page could plant an invite in a visitor's session (#163).

get.description:
Who is signed in, or null. Always 200: signed out is not an error (M4A.3).

It also hands out the CSRF cookie: every page asks this first, so the first write in a fresh
browser (a password reset opened from an email) carries a token (#234).

get.summary: A route to one or more goals
Topics matching the words someone types

get.description: Open drafts by default; `?state=submitted` is the review queue (M4R.6).

post.summary: Open a draft of a node

get.summary: Your review of the submitted revision

post.summary: Land a batch of approved drafts

post.description: The account and its history stay; it can no longer sign in, and its session ends.
